facts.text: Pedestrian Automatic Emergency Braking (PAEB) is the version of car AEB that detects people on foot and brakes for them.
facts.quote: Pedestrian Automatic Emergency Braking (PAEB) is the version of car AEB that detects people on foot and brakes for them.

facts.text: Pedestrian detection is harder than car detection because people are small, vary in shape and clothing, may stand, crouch or lie down, and are hard to see at night.
facts.quote: Detecting a person is harder than detecting a car. People are small, come in all shapes and clothing, stand, crouch or lie down, and are hard to see at night.

facts.text: Pedestrian AEB uses cameras, often with radar, and machine-learning software trained to recognize human shapes.
facts.quote: PAEB uses cameras, often with radar, and machine-learning software trained to recognize human shapes.

facts.text: The US rule FMVSS 127 requires pedestrian AEB to work between 10 and 73 km/h, in daylight and darkness.
facts.quote: The US rule FMVSS 127 requires pedestrian AEB to work between 10 and 73 km/h, in daylight and darkness

facts.text: Independent testing in October 2025 of four recent cars at 40 km/h found that nighttime pedestrian impact avoidance had improved from 0% in 2019 to 60% in 2025.
facts.quote: In an October 2025 test of four recent cars at 40 km/h, nighttime impact avoidance had improved from 0% in 2019 to 60% in 2025

facts.text: The October 2025 independent test of four recent cars at 40 km/h still found roughly 40% nighttime pedestrian impact-avoidance failures under ideal conditions.
facts.quote: still roughly 40% failures under ideal conditions

facts.text: In the October 2025 independent test of four recent cars at 40 km/h, high-visibility clothing caused a complete loss of pedestrian detection in some systems.
facts.quote: high-visibility clothing caused a complete loss of detection in some systems

facts.text: Caterpillar's own literature warns that its camera-based people detection may not detect people lying down or crouching, or when cameras are impaired by low light conditions (dusk, dawn, overcast) or inclement weather (snow, rain, fog).
facts.quote: Caterpillar's own literature says its camera-based people detection "may not detect people... lying down or crouching, or when cameras are impaired by low light conditions (dusk, dawn, overcast), inclement weather (snow, rain, fog)"

facts.text: People on foot are the main victims the heavy off-road machine Collision Mitigation System (CMS) must protect.
facts.quote: People on foot are the main victims the CMS must protect

facts.text: People on foot wear high-visibility clothing on every job site, and much job-site work happens at night.
facts.quote: they wear high-visibility clothing on every site, and much work happens at night

facts.text: The road record warns that pedestrian detection is the weakest and most condition-dependent part of the collision mitigation function.
facts.quote: The road record warns that pedestrian detection is the weakest and most condition-dependent part of the function

facts.text: The condition-dependent weaknesses of pedestrian detection in road evidence argue for retaining physical night and weather tests for heavy off-road CMS validation where simulation is weakest.
facts.quote: which argues for keeping physical night and weather tests where simulation is weakest
